name: Bradley Ridge (Bradley Ridge Apartments)
headline: Lincoln Avenue Communities is building Bradley Ridge, 336 two- to four-bedroom apartments in 14 buildings for households at or below 60% AMI, with an on-site Early Connections child care center, on 20 acres off Bradley Road southeast of the Colorado Springs Airport. It won a 2025 federal 4% credit award from CHFA backed by City of Colorado Springs bonds.
why_it_matters: The land sits with a nonprofit, the Pikes Peak Real Estate Foundation, which bought it with a $4.85M Prop 123 land banking award and leases it to the developer for $1 a year for 99 years. The city stacked its own bond cap with $12M of statewide balance to reach $76.8M of bonds.

status.label: Construction started (contractor post, December 2025); closing date not confirmed
status.detail: City Council passed the bond ordinance on 2025-09-09 and the city targeted a 2025-10-08 financial closing. CSI Construction Company posted on 2025-12-08 that it had broken ground. No public record found confirms the closing date or the land purchase. The city expects construction to be complete on 2028-01-10.

next_step: Watch for building permits and construction updates, the Early Connections center opening, and lease-up in 2028.

key_numbers.meaning: 168 two-bedroom, 84 three-bedroom and 84 four-bedroom units (924 bedrooms), with about 20 set aside for veterans.
About $70M over 10 years; no state credit.

key_numbers.value: $76,832,223 in City of Colorado Springs bonds
key_numbers.meaning: Capped at 52% of eligible basis: $64.8M of city bond cap plus $5M of fall 2024 and $7M of spring 2025 statewide balance (the latter through the Colorado Springs Housing Authority).
To the Pikes Peak Real Estate Foundation to buy the site; the largest award in the round announced 2025-05-07.

facts.value: CHFA prints Legacy Hill Drive & Bradley; the city's bond resolution places the site at the southwest corner of Bradley Ridge Drive and Bradley Landing Boulevard, Colorado Springs 80925 (Council District 4, near Bradley Road and South Powers)
Family, new construction; not in a QCT or DDA; in a SADDA; Section 8 column marked No
About 20 acres of vacant land; 14 buildings of 24 units each, plus a clubhouse, dog parks and open space

A standalone Early Connections Learning Centers center for children from 6 weeks old, with resident preference and sliding-scale tuition (infant care $228 a week against a $400 market rate). The city describes 8,500 sq ft for 60-65 children and 20 staff

About $1,514 a month for a two-bedroom per city presentations; the Gazette cites a $1,755 maximum for a three-bedroom at 60% AMI under CHFA's 2025 El Paso County limits, including utilities and parking
The city's market study figures put average market rents at $1,955 (2BR), $2,175 (3BR) and $2,573 (4BR), which are $440, $424 and $621 above the project's rents
Bradley Ridge Apartments LP, a Colorado limited partnership; general partner Bradley Ridge GP LLC, a Delaware LLC
At least 40% of units for low-income tenants during the qualified project period under the bond regulatory agreement (the tax credit restricts all 336 units to 60% AMI)

background.text: The Pikes Peak Real Estate Foundation buys the vacant parcel and handles groundwork, and Lincoln Avenue builds, owns and manages the apartments under a 99-year, $1-a-year lease. The Foundation said the land purchase was waiting on final bond approval.
City Council adopted Resolution 65-25 on 2025-05-13 declaring its intent to issue up to $76,832,222.72 of bonds, after a 2025-04-21 work session.

Council approved Ordinance 25-72 on first reading on 2025-08-26 and passed it finally on 2025-09-09, on the consent agenda; it was approved on 2025-09-12. The ordinance approves the indenture, loan agreement, bond purchase agreement, forward bond purchase agreement and tax regulatory agreement.
The city says it issues the bonds on behalf of the developer and is not liable for repaying them.
The Gazette reports that Lincoln Avenue's first affordable project in Colorado Springs was InterQuest Ridge in the north of the city.
El Paso County is short an estimated 16,000 child care slots for children under 5, which the child care center is meant to help address.
In May 2025 KKTV reported groundbreaking was expected in late 2025 or early 2026.

discrepancies.text: The city expects construction to be complete on 2028-01-10, while the Gazette reported a projected completion in March 2028 and a first phase opening in spring 2028.
The city's presentation targeted financial closing on 2025-10-08, while the Gazette reported a November 2025 target.
The city describes the child care center as serving 60-65 children from 6 weeks to 5 years old, while the Gazette reports 70 seats for children from 6 weeks to 6 years old.

The Gazette reported in May 2025 that Council had approved the $76 million bond, while Council records show that the May vote was only the inducement resolution and the bond ordinance passed on 2025-09-09.

Lease-up timing; an apartment listing site appears to advertise the property, but it could not be checked.
